The Bright Side:
The five-year-old child escaped physical injury, and NYPD officers rendered immediate first aid on scene. Independent Argus camera footage provides an objective factual record that prevents both agencies from erasing their tactical errors.

Federal agents used post-hoc justifications to rationalize reckless force, while city hall projected blame to harvest political capital. Neither side sought systemic solutions; both fed a cycle of manufactured conflict that sacrificed public trust.

The Unavoidable Truth: Firing seven bullets into a vehicle carrying a five-year-old child is indefensible.
The Unavoidable Lie: Demanding the release of a felony suspect was a genuine legal remedy rather than public theater.

When armed agents fire into a car carrying a toddler and politicians turn it into a megaphone duel, truth is abandoned. True governance protects the vulnerable first rather than treating human collateral as partisan leverage.

My heart aches for that terrified five-year-old boy sitting in shattered glass while bullets flew. No child should ever face such terror, and it breaks my soul to see adults reduce his survival to talking points instead of offering comfort and protection.

Bro, shooting seven times into a whip with a kid inside is completely wild. Then the mayor gets on the horn pretending he can just spring a guy facing felony heat? Everyone here is playing games while a toddler almost took a stray. Do better.

Stated Claim / Post Context:
Mamdani demands Trump release illegal immigrant shot by ICE agent as protests erupt in the Bronx

Mayor Zohran Mamdani demanded President Donald Trump release the man shot and injured by an ICE agent on Thursday in an incident that set off protests across New York City.

Actual Article Body:
This material may not be published, broadcast, rewritten, or redistributed. ©2026 FOX News Network, LLC. All rights reserved. Quotes displayed in real-time or delayed by at least 15 minutes. Market data provided by Factset. Powered and implemented by FactSet Digital Solutions. Legal Statement. Mutual Fund and ETF data provided by LSEG.

Demonstrators confronted law enforcement and filled the streets of the Bronx. (Credit: Peter Gerber for Fox News Digital)

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani demanded that President Donald Trump end all ICE enforcement in the state after a federal agent shot an illegal immigrant in the Bronx on Thursday, sparking protests and confrontations with law enforcement.

At a news conference late Thursday night, Mamdani condemned the shooting and said he spoke with Trump for about two hours following the incident.

Mamdani said he urged Trump to have the man released – an effort that was unsuccessful – and said New York City wants ICE agents out.

"All they do is terrorize this city," the mayor said of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.

ICE OFFICER SHOOTS, INJURES MAN DURING TARGETED IMMIGRATION OPERATION IN BRONX: DHS

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during a news conference after an ICE-involved shooting on Thursday. (WNYW)

Mamdani also accused ICE of acting "with impunity" and spreading "chaos and terror" across the country, alleging that ICE has killed more people than it has saved.

"Today's shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known," the mayor said.

"ICE is rotten to its core," he added.

Mamdani also confirmed that the man who was shot has been transported out of the hospital by ICE agents.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul also said she spoke to Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.

"Tonight, I spoke with President Trump and DHS Secretary Mullin about the shooting in Marble Hill," she said on X. "I expressed outrage on behalf of New Yorkers and urged them to halt ICE enforcement operations in New York. I also asked that any body camera footage of the shooting be released to the public so we can establish the facts and get to the truth."

ICE SHOOTING ROCKS AUSTIN AS DEMOCRAT DEMANDS BODYCAM VIDEO, INDEPENDENT PROBE

Protesters and law enforcement officers clash after a man was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer in New York on October 8, 2026. (CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images)

ICE was attempting to arrest a wanted man from the Dominican Republic at around 4 p.m. on Thursday when an agent opened fire and wounded him, according to DHS, which did not provide details on what led to the shooting.

"ICE officers immediately rendered aid. The individual is alive and at a local hospital. The FBI and HSI are on the scene. The incident remains under investigation. More information will be shared as it becomes available," DHS said in a statement.

DHS said the man, who was described as an illegal immigrant, had a prior grand larceny conviction and previous arrests involving assault, robbery, drug possession and weapons possession. The agency also alleged that he had ties to the Trinitarios gang.

Later Thursday night, New York City Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch identified the man as a 28-year-old and said a 5-year-old boy believed to be his son was inside the vehicle with him during the shooting.

"Based on evidence collected at the scene, we know that at least one ICE agent discharged the seven rounds, striking the driver in the neck below his left ear," Tisch said, adding that the boy was not injured and is in the care of a family member.

Protesters and law enforcement officers shove one another near where a man was shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer in New York on October 8, 2026. (CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / AFP via Getty Images)

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The agency said the man was arrested by New York City police on Dec. 7, 2023, but was released several days later. DHS blamed New York City's sanctuary policies for his release.

Hundreds of demonstrators gathered outside NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where the wounded man was being treated, and chanting "ICE off our streets" and "No justice, no peace." Protesters and police were seen shoving one another during the demonstration as officers began to set barricades, and some demonstrators threw water bottles at the officers.

"From Palestine to Mexico, all these walls have got to go," the group chanted.

Police made some arrests during the demonstration.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

Mamdani says he tried to negotiate release of wounded ‘criminal migrant’ shot by federal agent as he slams ICE as ‘rotten to the core’

Mamdani — who spoke over protesters' chants labeling him “complicit" - called ICE “rotten to its core.”

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said he tried to negotiate with President Trump to release the “criminal illegal alien” and alleged gang member who was shot by ICE Thursday in the Bronx as he called for the abolishment of the federal agency.

“Around 4 p.m. this afternoon, a New Yorker was shot by ICE agents in Marble Hill,” a furious Mamdani told reporters at the late-night press conference near the scene of a rowdy anti-ICE protest in the borough.

“For the past two hours, I’ve been on the phone with President Trump and [DHS] Secretary Mullin negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot. Those negotiations were unsuccessful,” Hizzoner said.

The migrant, identified by the NYPD as Oscar Belgal, 28, was shot in the neck and hospitalized before he was taken from NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital by unmarked ICE vehicles, according to the mayor.

Mamdani — who spoke over protesters’ chants labeling him “complicit” — called Immigration and Customs Enforcement “rotten to its core” and is an “agency that must be abolished” in the fiery speech.

“What does Trump have to say about all of this?” he demanded.

“Now I made clear to the president, to the secretary, our request [is] that ICE agents leave the scene entirely — as well as the demand that ICE stop its enforcement actions in New York City.”

The Department of Homeland Security said ICE had been attempting to arrest Belgal, of the Dominican Republic, who they claimed has ties to the Trinitarios gang when the shooting occurred.

“We know, and I have said this directly, whether to the president or to the public, ICE undermines public safety. It makes us less safe,” the mayor said.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch confirmed that seven rounds were fired by at least one ICE agent and made it clear that the “NYPD had no involvement in the federal operation prior to the shooting.”

Tisch said NYPD Argus cameras captured Belgal in the driver’s seat of a gray Honda CRV that was backing into a parking spot when a plain-clothes federal officer approached the driver’s side window with his gun drawn.

Another plain-clothes agent approached the driver’s side headlight when the vehicle began to move forward, out of the camera’s view, the commissioner added.

NYPD cameras didn’t capture the shooting, but Tisch said Belgal was struck in the neck, below his left ear.

A 5-year-old child, believed by police to be Belgal’s son, was inside the Honda CRV at the time of the shooting and was unharmed, Tisch said.

“There is no explanation for federal officers firing this many rounds into a car that has a 5-year-old in the car,” Mamdani said.

NYPD officers responding to a nearby call rushed to the scene for several reports of a shooting, the police commissioner said.

“When [officers] arrived, they encountered several men in various forms of attire, including some in construction-style vests, face masks, and at least one carrying a long gun,” Tisch said, adding, “officers also encountered the injured individual handcuffed and seated on the ground.”

Belgal was placed into an NYPD vehicle and was administered aid by officers before he was transported to NewYork Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where he arrived in stable condition, according to Tisch.

However, moments before the press conference kicked off around 11:20 p.m., “ICE put the man in an unmarked vehicle and whisked him away,” Hizzoner said.

“Let me say this plainly, what happened today was an outrage,” Mamdani fumed.

“Today’s shooting is only further devastating confirmation of what we have long known, which is that ICE operates with impunity, that they sow chaos and terror across our country, that they have killed far more of our neighbors than they could ever have claimed to save,” the mayor said.
